- Balaghat district in Madhya Pradesh faces a deadly convergence of measles, malaria, and malnutrition, provoking protests over the deaths of 26 Baiga tribal children. This year, malaria has produced 1,080 cases nationwide, including 329 in Balaghat—of which 307 are falciparum malaria, considered highly dangerous. article.articleHeadline: Scrub typhus cases in Odisha; Medical team sent
article.articleSummary:
- Odisha government has dispatched a medical team to Pallahara block in Angul district after scrub typhus was detected in Sanbagdhari village. In the last few days, rapid kit tests yielded 29 positives for scrub typhus, though these rapid tests are not confirmatory. A medical team from Angul conducted door-to-door surveys to identify additional suspected cases. Scrub typhus is an infectious bacterial disease transmitted by bites of infected larval mites. The report provides no laboratory-confirmed case counts or outcomes. The response focuses on surveillance and containment in Sanbagdhari and surrounding areas, with the affected locations listed as Odisha state, Angul district, Pallahara block, and Sanbagdhari village. Time reference: published 2026-08-30.

The Health Department has initiated precautionary and preventive measures, including active surveillance and other public health interventions, and states the situation is being closely monitored. article.articleHeadline: Drought can make disease outbreaks worse, and scientists now know why
article.articleSummary: Nearly two-thirds of the contiguous United States experienced drought in 2026, and UN counts say more than 77% of Earth's land has grown drier. Drought reshapes water availability, not just reducing it, and reorders interactions among people, wildlife, and disease vectors, amplifying outbreaks. In the Horn of Africa, drought followed by cholera outbreaks as displaced communities crowded around scarce water. In the western United States, a dry season coincided with a major avian botulism outbreak, killing more than 94,000 birds near Tule Lake. California’s 2013–2015 drought saw crowding around shrinking ponds and spikes in a waterborne frog parasite; later declines as habitats disappeared. Mosquito-borne viruses like West Nile and St. Louis encephalitis rose with drying. Valley fever increases with dust from dry conditions. In Indonesia, drought drove people to lower elevations, raising malaria deaths (554). Health agencies should monitor drought-driven changes around remaining water.

article.articleHeadline: No Cough or Fever but Positive for TB Bacteria? Get to Know Latent TB Infection: Okezone Women
article.articleSummary: Latent TB infection (LTBI) vs active TB in Indonesia. LTBI individuals have no symptoms; chest X-ray is usually normal and sputum tests are negative. Prof. Burhan notes LTBI bacteria are sleeping and present in small numbers, so health is unaffected, with no cough, fever, night sweats, or weight loss. Active TB typically presents with symptoms and positive radiographic or microbiological findings. article.articleHeadline: Vishwavani Health: HIV infections are increasing among Gen Z; what is the reason?
article.articleSummary: Published August 30, 2026: In an interview with Dr. Sutturu Malini, HIV is discussed as a virus of animal origin from Africa, believed to have crossed to humans from monkeys. HIV is an RNA retrovirus that attacks CD4 T cells, the key commander of the immune system. Once infected, the virus cannot be eradicated, but its progression to AIDS can be slowed with treatment; however, early infection may spread before symptoms appear. Transmission occurs mainly through sexual contact, blood, needles, and mother-to-child. The interview notes rising HIV infections among Gen Z in India, driven by sexual risk taking, influenced by social media, and increased sexual partnerships; historically low STI rates in India were linked to traditional family norms. Substance use, including cocaine, is cited as diminishing self-control and contributing to risk, along with lifestyle factors and diet. The emphasis is on awareness and risk reduction before intimate relationships.

Dr. Ram Ottalwar of the Bilaspur District Veterinary Hospital advocates vaccination campaigns in urban and rural areas and urges farmers to vaccinate on schedule and seek prompt medical care if symptoms appear. article.articleHeadline: Those days of fear from COVID; the nurse who cared for India's first COVID patient retires.
article.articleSummary: Lucy M. Sagheer, a public health nurse at Mathilakam Primary Health Centre in Thrissur, Kerala, retires after 31 years of service. She is remembered as the nurse who first cared for India’s initial COVID-19 patient, a girl from Mathilakam who had recently returned from Wuhan, China. On January 24, 2020 the patient arrived home; Sagheer attended her that evening, and COVID-19 was suspected due to travel history and symptoms. At that time there was no formal COVID protocol; the response followed Nip prophylaxis with home quarantine and immediate reporting to authorities. On January 27 the patient developed mild symptoms and was taken to Thrissur Medical College; COVID-19 was confirmed on January 30. The episode led to home quarantine for Sagheer and her husband, with three other PHC staff also quarantined. The article frames this as part of India’s early pandemic fear and the broader outbreak that followed.

article.articleHeadline: Monsoon Diet Tips: The Right Diet to Prevent Viral Fever - Learn from MGM's Dietitian What to Eat and What to Avoid

Women should focus on anemia- prevention with vitamin C–rich options (fresh papaya or pomegranate juice, apples, lemon water) and a herbal kadha; sprouts should be cooked or steamed. Elderly benefit from easy-to-digest options like golden milk (turmeric milk), oats or porridge, and increased ginger and garlic, while avoiding oily/spicy, stale, and raw vegetables. Emphasizes hot, homemade meals and boiled or lukewarm water due to humid conditions.

article.articleHeadline: Typhoid control needs more vaccine, less antibiotic
article.articleSummary: Typhoid cases are rising in India, but control relies on vaccination and diagnostics rather than antibiotics alone. Diagnosis is hindered by unreliable tests: Widal lacks specificity in endemic settings, and blood culture sensitivity is only ~55–60%, worsened by prior antibiotic exposure, fueling antimicrobial resistance and surveillance gaps. The WHO prioritizes typhoid-conjugate vaccines (TCV); India produced Typbar-TCV (WHO prequalified since 2017) and other Indian TCVs have prequalification, but vaccination scale remains inadequate within an integrated control strategy that also includes water, sanitation, and diagnostics. Key recommendations: strengthen surveillance with documentation of suspected and culture-confirmed cases and antimicrobial susceptibility; diagnostic stewardship—obtain blood cultures before antibiotics with adequate volume; invest in better rapid diagnostics; and revisit TCV’s role in public-health planning to achieve both vaccination and prevention.

article.articleHeadline: HU-UFSCar specialist warns about the risk of toxoplasmosis during pregnancy.
article.articleSummary: Toxoplasmosis during pregnancy is highlighted by a HU-UFSCar obstetrician in São Carlos, Brazil, after influencer Isabella Scherer disclosed a diagnosis at ten weeks. The infection, caused by Toxoplasma gondii, spreads mainly via cat feces, contaminated soil or water, and consumption of raw or undercooked meat or unwashed produce. It is relatively common in Brazil, but less frequent in the Southeast; maternal illness can be mild, while fetal risks include preterm birth, intracranial calcifications, vision or hearing problems, and developmental delay. Transmission depends on gestational age: earlier maternal infection lowers transmission but worsens fetal prognosis if transmission occurs; late infection increases transmission with milder fetal effects. Prenatal screening is routine; susceptible patients are re-tested. In São Carlos, treatment is available at CAIC, with HU-UFSCar handling notification, prescription, and follow-up. Prevention relies on hygiene: cook meat well, wash produce, wash hands, wear gloves for soil, and avoid cat feces exposure.

article.articleHeadline: Deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon accelerates the transmission of diseases.
article.articleSummary: Deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon accelerates transmission risk for leishmaniasis and Chagas disease. In Acre, northern Brazil, longer-deforested areas show greater abundance of flebótomos (sandflies) that transmit leishmaniasis, while landscapes with reduced forest cover increase the likelihood of triatomine bugs infected with Trypanosoma cruzi, the parasite behind Chagas. For leishmaniasis, vector abundance aligns more with the timing of deforestation and human occupation than with current forest cover. For Chagas, colonization of homes by triatomines is not required for elevated risk; deforestation alters the distance between palm trees and houses, and in highly deforested areas shorter distances correlate with more infected insects. Findings by Brazilian researchers led by Gabriel Laporta of the Federal University of ABC, and disclosed by FAPESP, were published in Parasites & Vectors and PLOS ONE, based on Acre field data.

SARI in under-2s declines, linked to fewer RSV hospitalizations; declines in other age groups tied to fewer influenza hospitalizations. Eight states remain at alert/risk/high risk without clear long-term growth: Amazonas, Mato Grosso do Sul, Minas Gerais, Paraná, Rio Grande do Sul, Rio de Janeiro, Santa Catarina, Sergipe. Capitals Aracaju, Belém, Boa Vista, and João Pessoa show ongoing SARI activity at alert/risk/high risk with long-term growth over six weeks. Nationally, 141,009 SARI cases in 2026, 54% lab-confirmed; 42% RSV, 30.4% rhinovirus, 17.9% influenza A, 5.4% influenza B, 3.9% SARS-CoV-2. COVID-19 incidence remains low; influenza A seasonality has ended.

article.articleHeadline: Brazil joins an international study on Hepatitis B.
article.articleSummary: Brazil joins an international study on Hepatitis B, led by Johns Hopkins School of Medicine, with partners in India, Senegal, and Uganda. article.articleHeadline: Seasonal water changes drive disease risk in Brazil's semiarid region
article.articleSummary: Three rural communities in Brazil’s Semiarid region (Quixeramobim and Quixadá, Ceará) study links between seasonal water changes and diarrhea risk. In 2025, researchers tracked water use across sources for households lacking public water supply, sampling in February, April, and September to bracket wet and dry seasons. Water sources included rainwater cisterns, hand-dug wells, surface reservoirs, tanker SISAR water, with samples tested for physicochemical parameters (temperature, ORP, alkalinity, electrical conductivity) and microbiology (total coliforms, E. coli). Diarrhea episodes were logged and analyzed alongside hydroclimate data using Kruskal-Wallis, Fisher’s exact, Cochran’s Q, and chi-square tests. 2025 rainfall fell sharply: Quixeramobim −35.2%, Quixadá −27.9% vs 2024, draining cisterns and prompting sharing with neighbors. As cisterns dwindle, drinking water remains prioritized while hygiene relies on more exposed surface sources, lowering water quality and increasing infection risk. ORP emerged as a key seasonal and community discriminator of water safety.

article.articleHeadline: The insect that coexisted with dinosaurs 66 million years ago and invaded homes to transmit worms dangerous to pets.
article.articleSummary: Fleas pose infection risks beyond itching. In dogs and cats, adult fleas are only about 5% of an infestation; eggs, larvae, and pupae develop off the host in bedding, carpets, gaps, and other pet-used spaces, sustaining cycles after adult fleas disappear. Transmission of Dipylidium caninum tapeworm occurs when a pet ingests an infected flea during grooming, with the parasite developing in the intestine. Females lay up to 50 eggs daily, and environmental stages persist weeks to months; the cycle runs about 21–28 days, depending on conditions. Fleas exhibit adaptations for parasitism: dorsally flattened bodies, ctenidia spines, specialized mouthparts, and hind legs enabling jumps up to 200× body length. Beyond tapeworms, flea feces can carry Bartonella henselae, linked to cat scratch disease in humans; thus control combines veterinarian-prescribed antiparasitics with thorough environmental cleaning, per Unesp Para Jovens and the US CDC.

article.articleHeadline: In Brazil, wild boars spread antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
article.articleSummary: Brazilian researchers tested 100 externally healthy European wild boars from two commercial farms in Goiás state, Brazil. The study, published in Archives of Microbiology, found Salmonella in one sample, with a strain lacking the virulence and antibiotic-resistance genes examined. Escherichia coli was detected in 56 of the 100 animals. Of 55 E. coli isolates tested, 98.2% showed resistance to multiple antibiotic classes, indicating widespread multidrug resistance among gut bacteria in farmed boars. This co-resistance raises concern for infection management in animals and potential implications for zoonotic transfer to humans. The findings highlight antimicrobial resistance in livestock and the need for surveillance of gut bacteria in farmed wildlife across Brazil. Published 2026-08-30.

article.articleHeadline: Heat and irregular rains call for vigilance against dengue, Chikungunya and Zika in Uberaba.
article.articleSummary: Uberaba remains at risk from Aedes aegypti during drought and irregular rainfall, with water-holding containers inside and around homes continuing to fuel transmission of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika. In 2026, the city reported 6,991 dengue notifications and 196 laboratory-confirmed cases, with no dengue deaths to date; these figures follow 26,014 notifications and 5,372 confirmed cases in the previous year. Authorities urge year-round vigilance: eliminate standing water in plant pots, drains, unused toilets, and water-storage containers; ensure water tanks are sealed; regularly inspect properties and clean gutters; discard tires, bottles, and other potential breeding sites. Dengue vaccination is free via Brazil’s SUS for eligible groups as a complementary measure. Uberaba’s Center for Endemic Diseases and Zoonoses participated in a regional Arboviruses Surveillance and Control meeting (Cisalp) to strengthen strategies for the upcoming season.

triage.triage_reason: ブラジル・ウベラバ市における季節性のデング熱等媒介感染症に関する定例的な予防啓発記事であり、2026年の症例数は前年より大幅減少し死亡例もなく、異常性や緊急性は認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Dangerous hand, foot and mouth disease in a 2-year-old child; doctors warn of complications to watch for.
article.articleSummary: Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease (HFMD) caused by Enterovirus 71 (EV71) surged in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. A 2-year-old was admitted to Children’s Hospital 2 with high fever, neurological signs and limb weakness; EV71 was confirmed. Despite IVIG, the child developed respiratory and circulatory complications, requiring PICU care, dialysis and mechanical ventilation, but recovered and was weaned off supports. Currently, about 20 HFMD patients, mostly aged 1–2, are hospitalized at Children’s Hospital 2. Dr. Vu Thi Tuy Dương notes two annual HFMD peaks (March–May and September–November), the latter aligning with school start and crowded settings. Delayed hospital presentation is common; families often treat fever at home before rash appears. At Children’s Hospital City, most admissions come from western provinces. Preventive advice emphasizes hand hygiene, food hygiene, environmental cleaning, isolation during illness, and prompt medical care for persistent fever, vomiting, irritability, or altered consciousness.

triage.headline_ja: 2歳児の重症手足口病、医師が合併症への注意を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: EV71による手足口病はベトナムで季節性に流行するホーチミン市の症例報告であり、重症例（ICU管理）はあるものの、例年の流行パターンの範囲内で国際的な異常性やIHR基準の該当は確認できないため、経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 毎年3-5月と9-11月に流行ピークがある季節性疾患であり、今回の報告は例年のパターンに沿うもの。EV71による重症合併症（呼吸・循環不全、透析、人工呼吸）が発生した個別症例が含まれるため、重症度トレンドの継続的な監視が望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: Dengue Snapshots
article.articleSummary: Dengue activity across Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Malaysia, Afghanistan, Vietnam and Cambodia remains high. Sri Lanka has 95,035 dengue cases and 72 deaths this year; August alone accounts for 9,699 cases, after July’s 29,962. The Western Province contains the majority (50,287 cases; 52.9%), with Gampaha (20,248; 21.3%) and Colombo (18,842; 19.8%) the most affected districts. In Bangladesh, nearly 1,100 new dengue cases and three deaths in the last 24 hours bring totals to 34,683 cases and 93 deaths; 2,402 patients are in treatment. Malaysia reports 42,848 dengue cases year-to-date with 34 deaths, a 34.8% rise in cases and 78.9% rise in fatalities. Afghanistan records 473 suspected July cases (up 85.5% from June) with no dengue deaths since January. Vietnam, July 2026: 15,940 cases and one death; Jan–Jul total 73,828 cases and nine deaths (1.3× 2025). Cambodia, early August: 54,697 cases and 72 deaths (CFR 0.1%), up 81.1% from 2025.

triage.triage_reason: デング熱は対象地域で季節性・流行地病であり、ベトナムでも症例数増加が報告されているが、突発的異常性や国際的拡大の兆候は明確でなく、経過観察が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: COVID-19 and Influenza Strike! Taiwan CDC Warns That Back-to-School Season Faces Four Major Infectious Diseases — Prevention Measures at a Glance
article.articleSummary: Taiwan CDC warns that the back-to-school period faces four major infectious diseases: COVID-19, influenza, enterovirus, and dengue fever. As of late August 2026, COVID-19 remains at a high plateau; last week’s visits reached 24,995, down 6% from the prior week, with 59 local severe cases and 19 deaths—the highest toll since last year’s season, with activity likely through September. Influenza activity has intensified, with weekly visits over 90,000; the dominant strain is A/H1N1. Enterovirus activity is stable; last week 6,546 ED/OPD visits, with Coxsackie A6 most common, followed by EV-D68 and Coxsackie A16. Dengue fever includes a domestic cluster in Kaohsiung; Changhua reports four dengue cases among about 100 Philippine study-tour participants across 17 counties; imported dengue totals 139 this year. Schools should reinforce hand hygiene, masking in crowded or poorly ventilated spaces, monitor for warning signs, and keep ill children at home; seek hospital if severe symptoms.

triage.headline_ja: COVID-19とインフルエンザが猛威！台湾CDCが新学期の四大感染症に警戒呼びかけ―予防策まとめ
triage.triage_reason: 台湾における季節性感染症（COVID-19、インフルエンザ、エンテロウイルス、デング熱）の定例サーベイランス報告であり、対象国リストに該当する国での発生ではないため見送りとする。
triage.notes: 記事は台湾国内の季節性感染症（新学期に伴う定例的な公衆衛生警告）に関するもの。彰化県で確認されたデング熱症例はフィリピン人研修参加者に関連するが、発生地は台湾国内であり、台湾は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations は空とした。

article.articleHeadline: Philippine study-tour group contracts dengue fever; four people in Changhua County diagnosed.
article.articleSummary: Four confirmed dengue fever cases in Changhua County, Taiwan, linked to a Philippine study-tour group that visited Cebu; the students recently returned and tested NS1-positive, with Taiwan CDC deeming them confirmed dengue cases and initiating close monitoring. The language school hosted about 100 students from 17 counties. Kaohsiung City Health Bureau reports nine related individuals: seven negative, two awaiting antibody testing. Taoyuan City Health Bureau notes 18 people under self-health monitoring; five sought care for cough or runny nose but rapid tests were negative; the remaining 13 are asymptomatic. As summer returns and the new school term begins, Changhua Health Bureau urges schools and parents to watch for fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, joint pain, rash, nausea, or fatigue, and to seek care and disclose travel history. Guosheng Elementary School principal Li Zhengying, who led a July Malaysia exchange, says precautions were taken and no infections occurred among students.

triage.triage_reason: 台湾（彰化県）における輸入デング熱の散発例であり、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響や異常性、国際的拡大リスクは認められない。対象国での発生でもなく社会的関心も限定的。

article.articleHeadline: 125 OFWs test positive for HIV in Q2 2026
article.articleSummary: 125 overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) tested positive for HIV in the second quarter of 2026 (April–June), per the Philippines Department of Health HIV and AIDS Surveillance report. In total, 124 of the new cases (99%) were acquired through sexual contact; one case lacked transmission data. By mode of sexual contact, 85 infections were among men who have sex with men; 15 involved both men and women; and 24 involved men and women. Since 1984, DOH records show 11,703 HIV cases among migrant workers. The report does not specify country of infection or export/import details. These figures indicate ongoing transmission linked to sexual contact among migrant workers, underscoring the need for targeted prevention, testing, and access to HIV services for OFWs in the Philippines.

article.articleHeadline: Mosquito ovitrap index remains elevated
article.articleSummary: Macau’s mosquito ovitrap index rose to 63.9% in August, above the five-year average of 59.4%, signaling increased risk for dengue and chikungunya transmission. Ovitrap readings topped 70% in Coloane, Fai Chi Kei, and the Inner Harbour area. With the school year starting, the Health Bureau urged schools and social service facilities to remove standing water and intensify environmental cleaning. Residents were advised to use repellents, wear long sleeves, and seek prompt medical care for fever, joint pain, or rash. This year Macau has recorded 10 imported dengue/chikungunya cases among travelers returning from Guangdong province, the Philippines, and Vietnam. Public health measures emphasize vector control and personal protection to mitigate spillover into the community.

triage.triage_reason: マカオの蚊媒介指数上昇と輸入デング/チクングニア症例の報告があるが、地域内での持続的なヒト-ヒト感染や重症例の情報はなく、予防的な公衆衛生対応の段階にとどまるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はマカオ（中国特別行政区）における蚊媒介指数の上昇と予防措置。輸入症例の由来地（広東省、フィリピン、ベトナム）は感染発生地ではなく渡航歴として言及されているため、China（マカオ含む）のみを発生地域として計上した。

article.articleHeadline: Over 490K children in CV still unvaccinated against measles, rubella
article.articleSummary: As of August 29, Central Visayas’ Measles-Rubella Supplemental Immunization Activity reached only 21.7% coverage, vaccinating 137,042 of 630,214 eligible children aged 6–59 months, leaving 493,172 unreached. The campaign covers Cebu and Bohol provinces and the cities of Cebu, Lapu-Lapu, and Mandaue; Cebu City had 18.4% coverage (16,636/90,604; 73,968 unreached). Cebu Province vaccinated 70,461 of 336,406 target (20.9%; 265,945 unreached). Lapu-Lapu City: 27.4% (13,394/48,856). Bohol Province: 22.3% (27,569/123,512). Mandaue City: 29.1% (8,982/30,836). The DOH extended vaccination to September 4 before returning to routine immunization. WHO classifies measles and rubella as highly contagious airborne diseases; symptoms include fever, cough, red eyes, rash, with pneumonia or encephalitis possible; transmission via respiratory droplets underscores need for sustained vaccination to prevent year-round spread.

article.articleHeadline: Brucker leads MSF's Ebola mission in the Congo | Kleine Zeitung
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, especially Nord-Kivu, where MSF runs a treatment center. Since May, over 5,000 infections and about 2,500 deaths have occurred; roughly one death every 30 minutes. No vaccine exists for this Ebola virus strain. MSF project coordinator Christoph Friedl, an Austrian psychologist, oversees staffing, safety, and logistics, coordinating with medical teams and authorities. Contact tracing is challenging and community knowledge about Ebola is uneven; health systems are overwhelmed. The report cites emotional moments: a young man with severe symptoms dies, while the first recovered patient exits the center through a dedicated door amid celebrations. Friedl expects to stay about three more months and return to Austria in early November.

article.articleHeadline: Jászberényi Sándor: Ebola is raging.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Congo is spreading rapidly, with the new Congo Ebola outbreak infecting more than 3,000 people in ten weeks. The virus is advancing faster than any predecessor, while the author notes a system that could have halted it has been dismantled. The piece blends reportage with stark, on-the-ground imagery of villages without running water or electricity and crowded urban markets, underscoring the threat as the outbreak penetrates communities. It evokes Africa’s security strains, including references to Boko Haram territory, to convey the gravity of the crisis. Clinical details are sparse in the article: no symptoms, laboratory confirmation, or death toll are provided. The narrative highlights critical background: the loss of an effective containment framework and the urgent need for a public-health response to this ongoing outbreak in the Congo.

triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で10週間に3000人以上が感染するエボラ出血熱の急速な拡大が報告されており、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが疑われるためフルRRAへの移行が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: A Russian man traveled to Egypt and contracted an unknown disease.
article.articleSummary: Russian IT professional, 30, contracted an unknown disease in Hurghada, Egypt, presenting anhidrosis (absence of sweating) as the first symptom, followed by a persistent heart rate up to 200 bpm, presyncope, dehydration, and later a gastrointestinal infection. Doctors in Cairo have not established a diagnosis; no laboratory confirmation reported. Family has been unable to return to Moscow for nearly a year, spending about $8,000 on examinations; the patient now relies on cooling routines (pouring water over himself) and avoids outdoor exposure, with work ability severely impaired. Visa expiry tensions and fines loom as the family plans to fly back to Russia to continue treatment there. The case remains unclassified, with source and transmission details undetermined. The report also notes a separate outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo where 14 people died within 19 days.

article.articleHeadline: Ituri: The Governor Announces Ebola Laboratories and Measures for Mambasa - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease resurgence in Ituri province, Mandima health zone, DRC, with 13 laboratory-confirmed cases and 10 deaths reported since the first confirmed case on June 15. Governor Kasongo Mulumba Batoka Gaby announced the urgent deployment of mobile Ebola laboratories and treatment centers in Mambasa territory to accelerate screening and care. The move follows civil-society briefings from Babila Babombi highlighting a triple crisis—health, security, and logistics—in the area; community engagement is urged to aid responses and protect medical teams. Insecurity persists, including August 26 incursions into the chiefdom capital and illicit roadblocks that hinder access and movement. The governor pledged to remove illegal barriers and conducted a planned field assessment to strengthen operations. Civil leaders will continue public awareness and alert systems in collaboration with authorities.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Kisangani: the Red Cross equipped with three jeeps, one of which is a medicalized ambulance - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Three jeeps, including a medicalized ambulance, donated by the IFRC to the Red Cross of the Democratic Republic of Congo in Kisangani (Tshopo) bolster the Ebola response, addressing early mobility challenges. The donation was welcomed by Provincial Health Division head Bienvenue Ikomo and Health Minister Simon Bokongo, who underscored transport as critical for containment. UN OCHA humanitarian affairs official Gustave Ngandu reiterated ongoing support to mobilize resources to end Ebola, while Franck Gefeu Molanga, provincial Red Cross president, called the vehicles a bulwark against Ebola. A fourth jeep from the same batch will be sent to Bas-Uele province and deployed starting Monday.

triage.headline_ja: キサンガニのエボラ出血熱：赤十字に医療用救急車を含む3台のジープが提供される - ACP

article.articleHeadline: Uganda marks end of Ebola disease outbreak - Uganda
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in Uganda ends after 42 days with no new confirmed cases; 20 infected, 18 recovered and 2 deaths, officially ending on 27 August. MSF, in collaboration with the Ugandan Ministry of Health, supported the response. MSF rehabilitated a 32-bed Ebola Treatment Unit in Mulago, Kampala, and renovated a 19-bed isolation centre in Bwera near the DRC. Teams trained Ministry of Health emergency staff and helped with infection prevention and control, isolation procedures, and case management across eight health centres. MSF has worked in Uganda since 1980 and remains active in Kasese district, running an adolescent-focused clinic. Beyond outbreak work, MSF provides sexual and reproductive health, chronic conditions such as sickle cell disease for people aged 9 months to 19 years, and social and mental health support for victims and survivors of sexual violence.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダ、エボラ出血熱の流行終息を宣言
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はウガンダにおけるエボラ流行の「終息」を報告するものであり、新規感染や拡大の懸念はない。また対象国リストにウガンダは含まれておらず、DRCは近隣国境施設の言及のみで実際の発生国ではない。

article.articleHeadline: TRIM22 blocks hepatitis B virus replication by tagging LDHA for destruction
article.articleSummary: TRIM22, an interferon-stimulated E3 ubiquitin ligase from Fujian Medical University, blocks hepatitis B virus (HBV) replication by tagging lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) with K48-linked ubiquitin and promoting its proteasomal destruction. This dual action suppresses glycolysis the virus relies on and relieves suppression of the RIG-I–MAVS innate sensing pathway, boosting antiviral signaling. In a study of 208 chronic hepatitis B patients, serum LDH levels correlated with HBV DNA levels and liver injury markers (ALT/AST), supporting a link between glycolytic activity and viral replication; LDHA was previously implicated in promoting HBV replication. In TRIM22-overexpressing cells, glycolytic gene expression and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) declined, with metabolomics showing glycolysis slows, resulting in reduced HBV replication. The work highlights host-directed strategies amid limited cure options for chronic HBV, where cccDNA persists despite antivirals and interferon therapy in China.

triage.headline_ja: TRIM22はLDHAを分解タグ付けすることでB型肝炎ウイルスの複製を阻害する
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は基礎研究（分子メカニズム解明）であり、公衆衛生上の緊急事態や発生イベントを報告するものではないため、トリアージ対象外。
triage.notes: 本記事は慢性B型肝炎の分子生物学的研究成果の発表であり、感染症のアウトブレイクや公衆衛生上のイベントを報告するものではない。中国・福建省の研究機関での基礎研究であるため、発生地域としての国は該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Hepatitis A vaccination proves crucial for prevention and outbreak control,
article.articleSummary: Hepatitis A vaccination is highly effective for both pre- and post-exposure prevention. A Czech-led systematic review (HAVETO) analyzed 21 studies (1985–2026) with laboratory-confirmed outcomes (IgM anti-HAV) and found pre-exposure effectiveness of 95.8% (20 infections among 925,238 vaccinated vs 1,029/1,708,753 unvaccinated) and post-exposure effectiveness of 96.9% (within 14 days of exposure; close-contact settings 95.3% and outbreak areas 98.4%). Vaccine platforms performed similarly: inactivated vaccines 97.2% in children; live attenuated vaccines in Chinese children 96.0%; randomized-child trials 97.5% (high certainty). An ecological analysis of 19 childhood vaccination programmes (1997–2024) estimated population impact at 83.9%, rising when pre-vaccination incidence exceeded 100/100,000. Coverage varied 40–95% but did not clearly explain impact; vaccinating young children appears to reduce transmission to adults, with Israel and Argentina cited as examples. Implications for outbreak control and shifting hepatitis A epidemiology.

triage.headline_ja: A型肝炎ワクチンは予防とアウトブレイク制御に極めて重要であることが判明
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はA型肝炎ワクチンの有効性に関するシステマティックレビュー（研究論文）であり、現在進行中のアウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の緊急事態を報告するものではない。
triage.notes: 記事はワクチン有効性に関するレビュー研究であり、イスラエル・アルゼンチン・中国は過去のワクチンプログラムの例として言及されているに過ぎず、現在の感染症アウトブレイク発生国ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Girl develops more than 20 warts all over her body after swimming for more than 20 days! Doctors warn: The pool is a high-risk area for transmission; don’t squeeze them with your hands.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-30, a girl in Henan Province, China was diagnosed with Molluscum contagiosum (MCV) after swimming for over 20 days, developing more than 20 pearly, dome-shaped papules across her trunk and limbs. Lesions are skin-colored to pearly white with a central dimple, size ranging from pinhead to green bean. Transmission occurs mainly via direct skin contact, contact with virus-contaminated items (towels, swim gear), or autoinoculation. Public pools and bathhouses are high-risk, as MCV can survive for hours in moist environments on pool edges, slides, and props. Wet skin and minor abrasions after swimming facilitate infection, especially in hot and humid late summer. Doctors warn against squeezing lesions, which can cause persistence, bacterial infection, scarring, or spread. Prevention: swim in licensed facilities, bring personal towels and gear, avoid swimming with wounds, rinse after swimming, dry thoroughly, and seek dermatology care for suspicious lesions.

article.articleHeadline: The seasons have disappeared... A midsummer outbreak of the common cold; Japan declares the flu a nationwide outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Aug 30, 2026: Korea reports rising SARS-CoV-2 activity with 9.1% positivity across sentinel clinics (week 33) and four straight weeks of higher COVID-19 hospitalizations (23→56). Predominant circulating lineages include BA.3.2, NB.1.8.1, PQ16.1.1 and RF.5. China experiences a July surge (~522,000 new cases) and influenza-like illness outpatients testing positive for SARS-CoV-2 at 21.2% across 1,041 surveillance hospitals. In Japan, the Ministry of Health declares a nationwide influenza outbreak in August—earlier than the usual winter season—recording 4,094 cases across roughly 3,000 sentinel facilities (threshold: at least 1 case per facility). Early flu onset is linked to extreme heat, humidity shifts, and indoor crowding. Officials warn that symptoms overlap with COVID-19 and summer colds, advocating vigilant testing, flexible public-health responses, and personal precautions during travel around holidays.

article.articleHeadline: The first pandemic in history: the plague that killed 50 million people and changed the borders of the world.
article.articleSummary: Plague of Justinian, the first documented pandemic, was caused by Yersinia pestis and likely originated in the Tian Shan mountains on the Kyrgyzstan-Kazakhstan-China frontier. From there it spread along land and sea routes to the Mediterranean, with Pelusium in the Nile delta marking the first documented entry into the Roman world around 541. Transmission occurred as infected black rats aboard grain ships carried fleas to humans. Procopius of Cesarea described sudden fever, buboes, delirium; at the peak Constantinople reportedly suffered up to 10,000 deaths per day (historians estimate closer to 5,000). Overall, 20-40% of Constantinople's population died, and mass graves were used. Economic and military effects were profound: grain shortages, tax revenue collapse, the Byzantine army weakened, facilitating Lombard invasion of northern Italy in 568. The plague contributed to the shift from Antiquity to the Middle Ages, with Arabs seizing Egypt and Syria in the 7th century.

article.articleHeadline: The habit of sharing razors can transmit HIV: Health Alert 2026
article.articleSummary: As of 30 August 2026, a Chinese health alert highlights HIV transmission risk from sharing personal grooming tools, illustrated by a Sichuan case where long-term shared razor use led to HIV infection. The risk arises when tools with blood contact create small skin abrasions during shaving, enabling bloodborne exposure. HIV is mainly spread via unsafe sexual contact, blood exposure, and mother-to-child transmission; routine activities like handshakes or shared meals do not spread HIV. Other high-risk scenarios include shared needles, tattooing, piercing, cosmetic tattooing, or invasive medical procedures in unsanitary settings with non-sterile instruments. Precautions include using personal items, selecting reputable facilities with proper infection control, and seeking prompt medical evaluation after potential exposure. Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) should be started within 72 hours when indicated, underscoring the need for rapid action rather than stigma toward people living with HIV.

article.articleSummary: On 28 August 2026, the WHO Global Center for Tuberculosis Research and Innovation was inaugurated within the China CDC. WHO TB chief Teresa Kasayeva said the center acknowledges China’s TB achievements and will provide a global platform to share experiences. China has achieved substantial declines in TB incidence and mortality since 2010, progress that outpaced the global average due to sustained investment, political will, and multisectoral action. China’s prevention approach combines timely diagnosis and treatment with expanded screening, active case finding, preventive interventions, and strong community engagement, embodied in its 'TB-free communities' model of early detection, preventive therapy, and smart management—cited by WHO as a global exemplar. The center will tackle multidrug-resistant TB and latent tuberculosis infection, and strengthen South-South and regional cooperation, BRICS TB networks, and Belt and Road collaboration to accelerate elimination, notably in high-burden, low-income settings. WHO expects deeper collaboration and wider global uptake of China's innovations.

article.articleHeadline: Dr. Yong advises isolating for at least 10 days if you contract COVID-19 | NEW TV
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 in Thailand: Thai virologist Dr. Yong Poovorawan advises infected individuals to isolate for at least 10 days from symptom onset to prevent transmission. Citing studies in JAMA and the New England Journal of Medicine, viable virus declines after day 7 and is rarely detectable after day 10, with the same infectious period for symptomatic, mild, and asymptomatic cases; vaccination status does not alter the duration, only viral load and test positivity. A practical approach: at least 7 days at home, with up to 3 additional days of caution if going out, maintaining precautions for the full 10 days. Antigen tests (ATK) often stay positive and should not solely determine when isolation ends due to lower sensitivity and possible false positives/negatives; routine retesting is discouraged to conserve resources.

article.articleHeadline: Girl dies after bathing due to pathogens: How safe are Bavaria's lakes?
article.articleSummary: Naegleria fowleri, the brain-eating amoeba, caused a fatal infection in eight-year-old Lilian Smart after a swimming outing at Lake Claiborne, Louisiana. The child contracted the amoeba nasally, allowing it to invade the brain and cause primary amebic meningoencephalitis (PAM). Globally, about 250 PAM cases are known, with many underreported. In Germany, no cases have been recorded; Bavarian lakes reach 30 C only after prolonged heat, with typical water temperatures in the mid-20s. The Robert Koch Institute notes that N. fowleri thrives in warm freshwater. Early PAM symptoms include headache, fever, nausea and vomiting, followed by neck stiffness, seizures and confusion. Travelers are cautioned to avoid submerging the head in warm waters, particularly in the southern United States, parts of South America, and southern Asia (India, Thailand), where infections are more common, with temperatures around 30–45 C in subtropics and tropics.

article.articleHeadline: Malaria: Why Global Warming Could Reduce Transmission in West Africa.
article.articleSummary: Malaria, caused by Plasmodium parasites and transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes, is reconfiguring across sub‑Saharan Africa as the climate warms. A July 2026 Nature study of 50,425 surveys from 1900–2016 links rising temperatures to differing malaria trends: transmission centered around 25°C, dropping below 16°C or above 34°C. In East and Southern Africa, warming likely increases malaria, while West Africa shows reductions, with about 5% fewer cases in Nigeria, Burkina Faso, and Mali and possible elimination in Niger, Gambia, Guinea‑Bissau, and Somalia. Conversely, cooler regions may see rises: ~5% in East African highlands (Ethiopia, Kenya, Burundi) and in Angola, Zambia, and northeast South Africa, with up to 20% in the Rift Valley and southern coast by 2100. The authors urge earlier anti‑malarial programs in warming regions and climate mitigation to keep warming below 2°C. In 2024, malaria caused about 610,000 deaths globally, ~580,000 in Africa.
